sections.html:
Dubuque sits on the Mississippi where Iowa, Illinois and Wisconsin meet, in the area known as the Tri-State Area. It is the Dubuque County seat and lies in the Driftless Area, a hilly region the last glaciation skipped. The city covers about 32 square miles and had 59,667 residents in 2020, which ranked it 11th in Iowa. Median age was 37.3.

Because of the terrain, slope is part of many lots. When you describe a Dubuque house to a buyer, include the grade of the lot and any drainage history. Settlement here began in 1785 and the city was incorporated on January 28, 1857, so plenty of houses are old, and the year yours was built is worth stating plainly.

Dubuque is usually described in four areas, each with its own housing history.

  • Downtown: the central business district, including the Fenelon Place Residential Historic District, Jackson Park, Old Main Street and the Millwork District.
  • North End: a working-class area settled by German immigrants in the late 1800s, close to Eagle Point Park, Lock and Dam No. 11 and Bee Branch Creek.
  • South End: historically Irish American, near St. Raphael's Cathedral and the Mines of Spain State Recreation Area.
  • West End: a suburban area developed after World War II, with Kennedy Mall, reaching toward Asbury and Peosta.

The North End sits close to Bee Branch Creek, so its flood history is the first thing a buyer will look up.

Dubuque has spent about $257.9 million on a flood mitigation plan built around the Bee Branch Watershed. The city lists two detention basins (2003 and 2009), restoration of Lower Bee Branch Creek (2011) and Upper Bee Branch Creek (2017), storm sewer upgrades and railroad culverts (2021) and a Healthy Homes program completed in 2022.

More is coming, including a gate and pump station expected around 2028, North End storm sewer improvements around 2029 and water plant flood protection around 2031. Funding included a $98.5 million Iowa Flood Mitigation Board award in December 2013 and $31.5 million in HUD resiliency funds in 2016.

Whether a particular house benefits is a parcel question. Ask the city and an insurer about your address instead of assuming protection.

sections.h2: The Bee Branch Healthy Homes loan
sections.html:
The Bee Branch Healthy Homes Resiliency Program gave eligible owners a five-year forgivable loan, recorded as a lien on the property. If you sell during those five years, repayment may be due.

Loan termHow it worked
InterestNone
Forgiveness20 percent per year over five years
Repayment triggerOwner sells, rents, transfers, vacates or abandons the property within the five years
Typical repairsFoundation work, sump pumps, drainage, mold remediation, furnace or water heater replacement, budgeted at an average of $15,067 per unit
OccupancyOwner-occupants had to keep the home as a primary residence for five years
  • Check your title report for a city lien from this program.
  • Ask the city for a payoff or forgiveness statement before closing.
  • Income limits were tied to 80 percent of area median income when the program ran.

Dubuque requires a rental license, and the city runs a licensing and inspection program for rental housing. Fees are $45 per structure, $45 per dwelling unit and $30 per rooming unit, with a $25 late payment charge.

Since March 1, 2024, the first licensing inspection is free. A re-inspection costs $100 per unit, and so does a no-show. Properties in good standing can self-inspect and self-certify every other two-year cycle, with self-certification done by July 1 and fees paid by March 1. Owners must also take a Successful Property Management Course offered at NICC.

Common violations involve alarms and stairs. Smoke alarms must be outside sleeping areas, inside sleeping rooms and on every story. Carbon monoxide alarms have been required since July 1, 2018 in units with fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces or attached garages. Handrails are required on stairs with four or more steps, and guards are required where a surface is 30 inches or more above grade.

Before you sell a rental that holds a city license, call Housing and Community Development or the Inspection and Construction Services office at 563-589-4100 to ask how the license is handled at a change of owner.

A house in a historic district may come with limits on exterior changes. Dubuque's Historic Preservation Commission protects historical and architectural resources, and city staff provide exterior design review. The commission has one seat for each designated historic district, and Fenelon Place and the Millwork District are among the downtown areas.

If you plan to change windows, siding or other exterior features before a sale, call the commission at 50 W 13th Street, 563-589-4100, to learn whether review applies. A buyer who takes the house as is would still follow the district rules.

sections.h2: Property tax and the transfer tax
sections.html:
The county treasurer mails Iowa property tax statements to the titleholder of record. The first half is due September 1 and the second March 1, with late interest starting October 1 and April 1. Taxes are normally prorated at a sale.

An owner who disagrees with an assessment can protest to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year, and the board cannot extend that window. Iowa's transfer tax is eighty cents per $500 above the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1).

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Dubuque
sections.html:
A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition and a title company settles taxes and liens at closing. That suits an inherited house, a rental you are tired of managing, or a house where flood repairs or an old city loan make a traditional sale slow.

  1. Describe the house, including slope, drainage and any flood history.
  2. Receive a written offer and decide whether it works.
  3. Gather the title report, tax statement and any city lien paperwork, such as a Healthy Homes payoff statement.
  4. Close with the title company, which records the deed and pays the liens from the proceeds.

You can say no and owe nothing, so compare the offer with the cost and time of listing.

A landlord ready to sell has a short list. Pull the rental license and the last inspection results, since a buyer will ask when the unit was last checked and whether anything was cited. Walk each unit for the usual violations, meaning smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, stair handrails and guards, and fix cheap items before anyone visits.

Decide what happens with tenants. A buyer can take the house with leases in place, or you can set a move-out date and close on an empty house. Either way, put the plan in writing and keep copies of every lease with the sale papers. If the license fees for the year are paid, keep the receipt too, so nobody argues about who owes a late charge.

faqs.q: How many people live in Dubuque?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 59,667 residents, which ranked Dubuque 11th among Iowa cities.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to rent a house in Dubuque?
faqs.a: Yes. The city licenses rental structures and units and inspects them. Fees are $45 per structure and $45 per dwelling unit.

faqs.q: What is the Bee Branch Healthy Homes loan?
faqs.a: It was a five-year forgivable loan, forgiven at 20 percent a year, for repairs in the Bee Branch Watershed. Repayment is due only if the owner sells or otherwise leaves within the five years.

faqs.q: Does Dubuque's flood project protect every house?
faqs.a: No. Protection depends on the parcel, so check yours with the city and your insurer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Dubuque house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy a house in its current condition, and a title company settles the taxes and liens at closing.
